ideas: Comparing the internet to things they already know
What they could actually use it for
Why it will matter even more for them later

phrases.meaning: a very big collection of information

phrases.phrase: at the touch of a button

phrases.meaning: talk while seeing each other online

model: My grandparents live in a small town in the countryside, and when I visited them last Tet, my grandmother actually asked me what the internet really is. So I tried to explain it in simple terms. I told her to imagine a huge library, which never closes, where you can find almost any information at the touch of a button. Then I said it's also like a giant post office, because you can send messages and photos to anyone in the world instantly. The part she liked most was that she could keep in touch with my cousin, who's studying in Australia. I showed her how to make a video call, and when she saw his face on the screen she was genuinely amazed. It took her a while to get the hang of it, but now she calls him every Sunday. I also told her she should be wary of strange messages asking for money, because scams are a real problem for older people. I think this kind of explanation really helps to bridge the gap between generations. Looking ahead, I'm fairly sure the internet is going to matter even more for them, because doctors will probably do more check-ups online. By the time I'm their age, we'll have technology I can't even imagine, and I might need my own grandchildren to explain it to me.
